# `molecule`

<!-- Generated by `vidgen gallery`; edit the sample in AGENTS.md (or video.yaml), not this file. -->

**Use it for:** molecules up close: DNA, RNAs, nucleosomes, receptors, channels, pumps, ATP synthase, ions (nm, notation checked); transport, diffusion, osmosis, action potentials.

A molecular close-up in nm: molecules in a solution or a membrane (the lipid bilayer with its two compartments named), each drawn to its textbook size — the DNA double helix with its 5′/3′ ends, base pairs and grooves; mRNA, tRNA, rRNA; a nucleosome, chromatin; proteins with domains; GPCRs, RTKs, gated channels, carriers, the Na⁺/K⁺ pump, H⁺ pumps, ABC transporters, aquaporins, ATP synthase; G proteins, kinases; ATP, GTP, cAMP, Pᵢ, glucose, water, O₂, CO₂, ions — with gene symbols in italics, protein names in roman type, charges as superscripts, modification markers (P, Ub, Ac, Me), labels of their parts and a scale bar. Orientations and places are checked. Solutes are drawn as particles at their concentrations; the actions set_state, transport, diffuse, osmosis and action_potential animate processes.

## YAML

From the author guide (`vidgen guide scenes`):

```yaml
- id: synthase
  type: molecule
  params:
    title: "ATP synthase"
    membrane: inner_mitochondrial                  # the bilayer between the intermembrane space and the matrix
    molecules:
      - {kind: atp_synthase, parts: true}          # F1 faces the matrix (faces: intermembrane_space is refused)
      - {kind: atp, in: matrix}
  beats:
    - text: "Protons flow back into the matrix through ATP synthase, turning its rotor, and F1 makes ATP."
```

## Params

| param | type | default | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | `str` |  | Title (in the header band at the top). (also: heading) |
| `membrane` | `str` | `'none'` | none (a solution) or the membrane across the view: plasma, inner_mitochondrial, thylakoid, er, bacterial, endosomal, lysosomal, golgi, vesicle, outer_mitochondrial (or a full name: plasma_membrane…). |
| `compartment` | `str` | `'cytosol'` | Without a membrane: the compartment the molecules are in (cytosol, nucleoplasm, matrix…), checked for each. |
| `cell` | `'animal' \| 'plant' \| 'bacterium'` | `'animal'` | The kind of cell (checked: no Na⁺/K⁺ pump in a plant, no nucleosomes in a bacterium); a thylakoid or bacterial membrane sets it. |
| `species` | `str` | `'human'` | Nomenclature for gene and protein names: human, mouse, rat, yeast, fission_yeast, fly, zebrafish, e_coli, arabidopsis. |
| `molecules` | `list[str \| MoleculeItem]` |  | The molecules: a kind, or {kind, id, at, state, label, gene, protein, parts, ...}. |
| `molecules.kind` | `str` | required | dna, mrna, trna, rrna, nucleosome, chromatin, protein, kinase, phosphatase, g_protein, gpcr, rtk, ion_channel, carrier, na_k_atpase, h_atpase, abc_transporter, aquaporin, atp_synthase, atp, adp, pi, gtp, gdp, camp, glucose, ligand, ion, water, o2, co2, drug. |
| `molecules.id` | `str \| None` |  | Its name for actions (default: the kind, kind_2 for a second). |
| `molecules.at` | `float \| tuple[float, float] \| None` |  | Where its middle is, in nm from the view's middle: a membrane protein x along the membrane; others [x, y] (y up: the membrane's exoplasmic side); default laid out in a row. |
| `molecules.angle` | `float \| None` |  | Turn in degrees (not membrane proteins: they keep their orientation). |
| `molecules.in` | `str \| None` |  | A soluble molecule's compartment (extracellular, cytosol, matrix…): the side of the membrane it is on (checked: DNA in the nucleoplasm, cAMP in the cytosol). |
| `molecules.faces` | `str \| None` |  | A membrane protein: the compartment its oriented part faces (ATP synthase F₁: matrix; a GPCR's N-terminus: extracellular); checked. |
| `molecules.state` | `str \| None` |  | Its state at the start (set_state changes it): gpcr / g_protein: inactive or active; rtk: monomer or dimer; ion_channel: closed, open or inactivated; carrier: outward, occluded or inward; na_k_atpase and h_atpase: e1, e1p, e2p or e2; abc_transporter: inward or outward; atp_synthase: synthesis or hydrolysis; kinase: active or inactive; chromatin: 10nm or compact. |
| `molecules.label` | `str \| bool \| None` |  | Its name under it (default: the kind's, or the gene / protein given); false for none. Pango markup: <i>, <sup>, <sub>. |
| `molecules.gene` | `str \| None` |  | A gene symbol (italic, checked against the species' nomenclature: human TP53, mouse Trp53, yeast CDC28). |
| `molecules.protein` | `str \| None` |  | A protein name (roman: TP53 or p53; mouse TRP53; yeast Cdc28). |
| `molecules.species` | `str \| None` |  | For gene and protein: human (default: the scene's), mouse, rat, yeast, fission_yeast, fly, zebrafish, e_coli, arabidopsis. |
| `molecules.parts` | `bool \| list[str] \| None` |  | Name its parts with leader lines (true, false or names); default true when it is the only molecule. |
| `molecules.bp` | `int \| None` |  | DNA: base pairs (default 21, two turns). |
| `molecules.sequence` | `str \| None` |  | DNA: the top strand 5′→3′ (its partner is drawn antiparallel); mRNA: its sequence (ACGU). |
| `molecules.letters` | `bool \| None` |  | DNA, mRNA: write the bases (default when a sequence is given). |
| `molecules.anticodon` | `str \| None` |  | tRNA: its anticodon 5′→3′ (CAU reads the codon AUG); checked against amino_acid. |
| `molecules.amino_acid` | `str \| None` |  | tRNA: the amino acid on its 3′ CCA end (Met, Phe…). |
| `molecules.style` | `'cloverleaf' \| 'l_shape' \| None` |  | tRNA: cloverleaf (secondary structure, default) or l_shape (3-D shape). |
| `molecules.rrna` | `str \| None` |  | rRNA: 18S, 28S, 5.8S, 5S, 16S, 23S, 12S. |
| `molecules.marks` | `list[str]` |  | Nucleosome: histone marks (H3K4me3, H3K27ac, H3K9me3, H4K16ac, H2AK119ub, H3S10ph), checked against the histone sequences. |
| `molecules.nucleosomes` | `int \| None` |  | Chromatin: how many nucleosomes. |
| `molecules.domains` | `list[str]` |  | Protein: its domains' names (SH2, kinase…), one lobe each. |
| `molecules.mass` | `float \| None` |  | Protein: its mass in kDa (sets its size; 50 kDa is about 5 nm). |
| `molecules.ligand` | `bool \| None` |  | gpcr: a ligand in its pocket; ion_channel with ligand gating: bound when open. |
| `molecules.gating` | `'voltage' \| 'ligand' \| 'mechanical' \| None` |  | ion_channel: what opens it (default voltage). |
| `molecules.ion` | `str \| None` |  | ion_channel: the ion it passes (K+, Na+, Ca2+, Cl-); ion: which ion (Na+, K+, Ca2+, Cl-, H+, Mg2+). |
| `molecules.mode` | `'uniport' \| 'symport' \| 'antiport' \| None` |  | carrier: one solute, two the same way, two opposite ways. |
| `molecules.transporter` | `str \| None` |  | carrier: a named carrier that sets mode, substrates, moves and ratio: glut1, glut4, sglt1 (2 Na⁺ + glucose in), sglt2, ncx (3 Na⁺ in, Ca²⁺ out), nhe1, nkcc1, kcc2. |
| `molecules.substrates` | `list[str]` |  | carrier: its solutes (Na+, glucose, H+, Ca2+…); abc_transporter: its one substrate (default drug). |
| `molecules.moves` | `list['in' \| 'out']` |  | carrier: the way each solute moves (in: into the cytosol); abc_transporter: out (export, default) or in (bacterial importers only). |
| `molecules.ratio` | `list[int]` |  | carrier: how many of each substrate per cycle ([2, 1]: 2 Na⁺ per glucose). |
| `molecules.c_subunits` | `int \| None` |  | atp_synthase: c subunits in its ring (default by membrane: 8 mitochondria, 14 chloroplasts, 10 bacteria). |
| `molecules.cap` | `bool \| None` |  | mRNA: the 5′ cap (default true). |
| `molecules.tail` | `bool \| None` |  | mRNA: the poly(A) tail (default true). |
| `molecules.modifications` | `list[str \| Modification]` |  | Markers on a protein: P, Ub, Ac, Me, each with its residue ({mark: P, at: Ser15}). |
| `molecules.modifications.mark` | `'P' \| 'Ub' \| 'Ac' \| 'Me'` | required | P (phosphorylation: Ser, Thr, Tyr), Ub (ubiquitin: Lys), Ac (acetyl: Lys), Me (methyl: Lys, Arg). |
| `molecules.modifications.at` | `str \| None` |  | The residue: Ser15 or S15 (checked: phosphate never on Lys). |
| `molecules.modifications.domain` | `str \| None` |  | A protein's domain the marker sits on (one of its domains), e.g. kinase. |
| `solutes` | `list[str \| Solute]` |  | Free particles at their concentrations on each side: a solute (K+) or {solute, mM: {extracellular: 5, cytosol: 140}, id, count}. |
| `solutes.solute` | `str` | required | An ion (Na+, K+, Ca2+, Cl-, H+, Mg2+) or a small molecule (glucose, water, o2, co2, atp, drug…). |
| `solutes.id` | `str \| None` |  | Its name for actions (default: sodium, potassium, calcium, chloride, protons, magnesium, or the molecule's name). |
| `solutes.mM` | `dict[str, float]` |  | Concentration (mM) on each side: the membrane's two compartments ({extracellular: 5, cytosol: 140}), or left and right without a membrane; default: the typical values of a mammalian cell's plasma membrane. |
| `solutes.count` | `int` | `12` | Particles drawn on the more concentrated side (the other side in proportion; none below 1 % of it). |
| `potential` | `float \| None` |  | The membrane potential (mV, the cytosolic side relative to the other: −70 for a resting neuron): a live readout and the membrane's charges; default: none (−70 assumed at the plasma membrane for gradients). |
| `bars` | `bool` | `True` | With solutes: their concentrations on each side as bars with values (they change with diffuse and osmosis). |
| `width` | `float \| str \| None` |  | What the view spans across the body's shorter side ('30 nm'); default: fits the molecules. |
| `sides` | `bool` | `True` | Name the compartments on either side of the membrane. |
| `labels` | `bool` | `True` | Name the molecules (under each) and their parts (see parts). |
| `scale_bar` | `bool` | `True` | A scale bar in nm. |
| `reveal` | `'all' \| 'per_beat'` | `'all'` | all: everything in the first beat; per_beat: the membrane, then one molecule per beat. |
| `seed` | `int` | `1` | Changes where particles start and the random walks they take. |
| `title_size` | `size` | `'heading'` | Title size. (also: heading_size) |
| `label_size` | `size` | `'caption'` | Size of the labels and the scale bar's text. |
| `gene` | `GeneParams \| None` |  | A gene whose expression the scene shows (then no molecules, solutes or membrane): {codons, introns, signal_peptide, glycosylation, seed} or {sequence, introns: [[start, end]]} or {protein}; its steps are actions (transcribe: gene). |
| `gene.id` | `str` | `'gene'` | Its name for actions (transcribe: gene). |
| `gene.name` | `str \| None` |  | The gene's symbol (italic; checked against the species' nomenclature: human INS, mouse Ins2). |
| `gene.product` | `str \| None` |  | The protein's name (roman; checked like a molecule's protein). |
| `gene.species` | `str \| None` |  | For name and product: human (default: the scene's), mouse, rat, yeast… |
| `gene.sequence` | `str \| None` |  | The coding strand of the transcribed region, 5′→3′ from the transcription start (+1), DNA (ACGT): 5′ UTR, exons and introns, 3′ UTR with the poly(A) signal AATAAA. |
| `gene.introns` | `int \| list[tuple[int, int]] \| None` |  | With a sequence: their positions [[start, end], …] (1-based, inclusive; each must start GT and end AG); with protein or codons: how many (generated: GU…branch A…AG). |
| `gene.protein` | `str \| None` |  | The protein (one-letter MALW… or three-letter Met-Ala-Leu…): the gene is written for it (frequent human codons); with a sequence: checked against what it encodes. |
| `gene.codons` | `int \| None` |  | A generated protein of this many codons (Met included, the stop codon not); default 12 (72 with a signal peptide). |
| `gene.signal_peptide` | `bool` | `False` | Generated: start with a cleavable signal peptide (n-, h- and c-region); written: checked that it has one. |
| `gene.glycosylation` | `bool` | `False` | Generated: an N-glycosylation sequon (Asn-X-Ser/Thr) after the signal peptide; written: checked. |
| `gene.seed` | `int` | `1` | Changes a generated gene's sequence. |
| `gene.start` | `'dna' \| 'mrna'` | `'dna'` | What the scene shows at first: dna (the gene in the nucleus) or mrna (a mature mRNA in the cytosol, ready to be translated). |
| `gene.codes` | `'three' \| 'one'` | `'three'` | Amino acids as three-letter (Met) or one-letter (M) codes. |
